load_order.reason: Foundational object. Holds default values (Inventory Source, Eng Type, Lot/Serial Tracking, Planning Policy, costing weights, lead times, etc.) that propagate to Engineering Item Master records via the rstk__peitem_iccomcod__r external ID foreign key. Must exist in Rootstock before any peitem record can reference it.

Every peitem record requires a valid iccomcod external ID via rstk__peitem_iccomcod__r. Loading peitem before iccomcod will cause every row to fail validation on the FK lookup. Per the peitem schema doc: 'The Inventory Commodity Code record must exist before adding the Engineering Item Master for the respective Inventory Division.'

entries.explanation: A label that appears on the first row of each assembly in the Engineering BOM Masters, formatted as '<Assembly>-<CaseQuantity>' (for example, 'P-DWS-1000' indicates the P-DWS assembly with 1,000 units per case). Despite the name, this is not a Rootstock commodity code — it is a header marker used by the source system. The information it carries is already available in Assy Item and ProductCaseQty.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If desired, parse the case quantity portion (the suffix after the last hyphen) and use it to cross-validate against ProductCaseQty in the Products table.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Inventory Commodity Code), External ID, Required.

Drives commodity code routing for raw materials and components that exist in the Engineering BOM Masters but not in Products (~68 items: inks, glues, paper sheets, boxes, tape). 'Non Inventory' indicates consumables that should not be MRP-planned (inks coded A0xxx, glues coded D0xxx/C0xxx). 'Inventory' indicates stock-tracked raw materials that do need planning (paper PR-*, boxes BX-/BC-/N0-*, stadium cup blanks WSC*).

Note: this Engineering BOM Masters field has different semantics from the Engineering Item Master.Item Type field, which uses Direct Material / Labor Only — the picklists do not align.

External ID format: all outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2) per schema requirement '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'.
transformations:
Apply only to SKUs that appear as Engineering BOM Masters.Part # but not as Products.ProductSKU:

  WHEN Engineering BOM Masters.Item Type = 'Non Inventory':
    IF Part # matches /^A\d{4}/                          → '2_RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK'
    IF Part # matches /^D\d{4}|^C\d{4}/                  → '2_RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE'  (D0001, C0026 etc. — glues, not inks)
    IF Part # matches /^H\d{4}|TAPE|LABEL/ OR = 'BCI'    → '2_RCB-PACKAGING'         (BCI = printed instructions)
    ELSE                                                  → '2_RCB-UNROUTED'         (explicit catch-all, requires human review)

  WHEN Engineering BOM Masters.Item Type = 'Inventory':
    IF Part # LIKE 'PR-%' OR contains 'SBS'/'KRA'         → '2_RCB-PRINT-MAT'        (paper raw material)
    IF Part # LIKE 'BX-%'/'BG-%'/'S-%'/'BC%'/'N0%'        → '2_RCB-PACKAGING'        (boxes, bags incl. BCB-*/BCK-*/BCW-*/N0068)
    IF Part # LIKE 'WSC%'                                 → '2_RCB-BLANK-CUP'        (stadium cup blanks WSC22/WSC32)
    ELSE                                                  → '2_RCB-UNROUTED'         (explicit catch-all, requires human review)

All outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2). Items routed to RCB-UNROUTED must be reviewed by the user before load — silent fallback to a default category is not used.

entries.explanation: Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call: Item Number is sourced from Products.ProductSKU exclusively, because every item including BoM parents appears in the Products file (RCB's item master). The Engineering BOM Masters Assy Item column is redundant for Item Number and not mapped. Note: the Manufactured-vs-Purchased distinction (which previously relied on Assy Item presence) is preserved via the InvMasterSKU → Inventory Source mapping, which still tests for BoM presence. VERIFY before load: spot-check that BoM parents all appear in Products.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. Item Number comes from Products.ProductSKU, per Joanna (Jun 5). Note: Inventory Source still uses BoM-presence to flag Manufactured items (see InvMasterSKU → Inventory Source).

entries.explanation: Per the business context document, the Info column carries the Parent Product identifier for the assembly. The format `<Parent SKU>, <CaseSize>` (e.g., 'P-DWS, 1 Case (1000 Sleeves)') prefixes each Engineering BOM Masters row with its parent finished-good reference, anchoring every component row to its assembly. For the two target tables in scope (Engineering Item Master and Inventory Commodity Code), the parent-product relationship is not a field — these are item-level tables, not relationship tables. The Parent SKU itself is already cleanly available as the Assy Item column; the Info column repackages it with case-size context that would be needed on a future BoM-header or BoM-relationship migration.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future BoM-header migration phase where the parent-product reference and case-size context will be needed.

entries.explanation: Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call: the Products file (which is RCB's item master) carries ProductName for all items, including BoM components, so item descriptions come from Products exclusively. The Engineering BOM Masters Assy Desc column is redundant and not mapped. VERIFY before load: this assumes every BoM component also appears in the Products file. Prior data review suggested ~68 components (raw paper PR-*, inks A0xxx, glues D0xxx, boxes BX-*) may exist only in the BoM — if so, those items would lose their description source. Spot-check that BoM components appear in Products.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. Item Description is sourced from Products.ProductName exclusively, per Joanna (Jun 5).

entries.explanation: Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call: Item Number is sourced from Products.ProductSKU exclusively, because every component appears in the Products file (RCB's item master). The Engineering BOM Masters Part # column is redundant for Item Number and not mapped. VERIFY before load: this is the highest-risk of the four BoM unmappings — prior data review suggested ~68 components (raw paper PR-*, inks A0xxx, glues D0xxx, boxes BX-*, tape) may exist ONLY in the BoM and not in Products. If that is correct, unmapping Part # drops those items from the migration entirely. Spot-check before proceeding.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. Item Number comes from Products.ProductSKU, per Joanna (Jun 5). CAUTION: if BoM-only components exist (not in Products), they are dropped by this change — verify first.

entries.explanation: Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call: item descriptions come from Products.ProductName exclusively, because the Products file (RCB's item master) covers all items including BoM components. The Engineering BOM Masters Item description column is redundant and not mapped. VERIFY before load: assumes every BoM component appears in Products — spot-check the ~68 potentially BoM-only components (raw paper, inks, glues, boxes).
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. Item Description comes from Products.ProductName, per Joanna (Jun 5).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Standard, Phantom, Reference}, Optional (inherits from commodity code if blank).

Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call, Eng Type is derived from two structural signals rather than a dedicated source column:
  • Reference items are identified by BOM Quantity = 0 (RCB convention — reference items appear in BoMs at zero quantity to indicate they are referenced but not consumed). Joanna is providing a business context document explaining this convention.
  • Phantom items are identified by a SKU appearing as both Assy Item (parent) and Part # (component) — sub-assemblies never independently inventoried (8 SKUs in the current data: B-CHC08/12/16/20, WHC08/12/16/20).
  • Everything else defaults to Standard.

This replaces the prior Sub-Assembly Flag → Eng Type mapping, which Joanna confirmed is not a usable source. Confidence is held at 70 pending Joanna's context document confirming the BOM Quantity = 0 convention.
transformations:
CASE
  WHEN SKU IN (SELECT "Assy Item" FROM "Engineering BOM Masters")
   AND SKU IN (SELECT "Part #" FROM "Engineering BOM Masters")
  THEN 'Phantom'
  WHEN "BOM Quantity" = 0
  THEN 'Reference'
  ELSE 'Standard'
END

The Phantom check runs first (a structural property of the SKU, true regardless of quantity). The Reference check runs second on the BOM Quantity = 0 convention. Standard is the default. Phantom and Reference items keep their underlying Inventory Source (Manufactured for assemblies); only Eng Type changes. Pending Joanna's business context document confirming the BOM Quantity = 0 = Reference convention.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Required.

Per-component engineering UOM in the Engineering BOM Masters (Sheet, 5Kg, Gallon, Each, Roll, Linear FT, Lbs, Liter). This drives the Eng UOM for components extracted from Engineering BOM Masters.Part #. Parent assemblies (finished cups and sleeves) are always counted as Each and use a hardcoded EA value — they do not pull from this field.

UOM code corrections confirmed by Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call: Roll → RL (not ROLL), Liter → LTR (not L). Joanna is providing the UOM reference file (export of the target org's UOM master) to validate all codes and surface any remaining mismatches.
transformations:
For components extracted from Engineering BOM Masters.Part #, look up the source UOM and map to Rootstock UOM external ID:

  Sheet     → SHEET
  5Kg       → KG    (note: '5Kg' is the pail size, not a unit — confirm with RCB whether inks should be tracked in KG by weight or in pails as Each)
  Gallon    → GAL
  Each      → EA
  Roll      → RL    (corrected from ROLL per Joanna, Jun 5)
  Linear FT → FT
  Lbs       → LB
  Liter     → LTR   (corrected from L per Joanna, Jun 5)

UOM codes confirmed against the Rootstock target org per Joanna (Jun 5); the forthcoming UOM reference file will validate the full set. For parent assemblies extracted from Assy Item, hardcode EA. Pre-create any missing UOM records in Rootstock before loading.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Required.

Default engineering UOM at the commodity code level. Items inherit this default unless overridden at the item level. Set once per commodity code, derived from the most common UOM among the items in that code. Manufactured codes (printed cups, sleeves) use EA. Raw-material codes use the source UOM — paper codes use SHEET, ink codes use KG.
transformations:
Group items by their assigned commodity code, take the most common UOM among them, and map to a Rootstock UOM external ID. Per-commodity-code constant. Recommended values for RCB:

  RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK,
  RCB-STOCK-RESALE, RCB-PACKAGING, RCB-APPAREL-DROP  → EA
  RCB-PRINT-MAT       → SHEET
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK  → KG

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Required.

Default inventory UOM — how RCB tracks stock for items in this commodity code. Reference data shows EA across all codes because cups, sleeves, blanks, boxes, and drop-ship items are all counted in whole units. Override to a bulk unit (KG) only for consumables tracked by weight, such as inks.
transformations:
Default to EA. Override per commodity code only where bulk weight tracking applies:

  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK → KG
  All other codes    → EA

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Conditionally Required.

Default purchasing UOM — how RCB buys items in this commodity code. Finished and stock items are purchased in Each. Raw materials and consumables are purchased in their bulk forms (paper by the SHEET, ink by the KG, tape by the ROLL).
transformations:
Group items by commodity code and take the most common purchasing UOM among them. Recommended values:

  RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK,
  RCB-STOCK-RESALE, RCB-PACKAGING, RCB-APPAREL-DROP  → EA
  RCB-PRINT-MAT       → SHEET
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK  → KG

entries.explanation: Per-finished-unit consumption (for example, 0.0625 sheets per sleeve, or 0.00000005 kg of ink per cup). This belongs on the BOM Component record that links a parent to its components with quantities, not on the Engineering Item Master or Inventory Commodity Code tables in the current migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future BOM Component migration phase.

entries.explanation: Per-component cost contribution from the Engineering BOM Masters source (for example, $0.02 per sheet). This belongs on Item Cost or BOM Cost records, not on the Engineering Item Master or Inventory Commodity Code tables in the current migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future cost migration phase.

entries.explanation: Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call: RCB's source data does not contain a Sub-Assembly Flag suitable for driving Eng Type. The Eng Type distinction (Standard / Phantom / Reference) is derived from other signals instead — see the BOM Quantity → Eng Type mapping, which uses BOM Quantity = 0 to detect Reference items and the structural parent-and-component test to detect Phantom items. This source field is not loaded.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. Eng Type is populated from BOM Quantity and the structural sub-assembly test instead (see the BOM Quantity → Eng Type mapping).

entries.explanation: Internal numeric primary key from the source system (Prosys). It has no business meaning outside Prosys and is not needed in Rootstock, which generates its own internal IDs.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If audit traceability back to Prosys is required, optionally preserve in a custom field.

entries.explanation: Foreign key linking each product to a WooCommerce entry (RCB's e-commerce platform). Relevant only if RCB plans to keep the WooCommerce integration after migration. If not, this field has no destination in Rootstock.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If RCB intends to maintain the WooCommerce integration, preserve in a custom field for the integration layer to use.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(50), Required.

The primary business SKU used across orders, purchase orders, and invoices. Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call, the Products file is RCB's item master and is the sole source for Item Number (the Engineering BOM Masters Assy Item and Part # sources have been unmapped). Each distinct ProductSKU becomes one Engineering Item Master record, producing ~4,587 EIM records.

**Decision point — EIM grain.** RCB's current production Rootstock org has only 338 EIM records, a curated subset closer to InvMasterSKU grain (~386 unique non-sentinel values). Two defensible approaches:
  (a) ProductSKU grain (~4,587 EIMs) — the default; treats every Products row as a distinct item.
  (b) InvMasterSKU grain (~386 EIMs) — matches the prod org pattern.
Confidence is held at 55 to surface this as a decision RCB needs to make.

Additional consideration: ProductSKU has 622 duplicate values across 1,873 rows (32% of file). See the transformation for dedup logic.
transformations:
Apply dedup before extracting Item Number:

  WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT ProductSKU, ProductName, InvMasterSKU, ProductActive, ProductUpdated,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
             PARTITION BY TRIM(ProductSKU)
             ORDER BY 
               CASE WHEN InvMasterSKU IS NOT NULL AND InvMasterSKU NOT IN ('NO INVENTORY','OUTSOURCED') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
               ProductActive DESC,
               ProductUpdated DESC NULLS LAST
           ) AS rn
    FROM products
  )
  SELECT TRIM(ProductSKU) AS item_number FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1

Tiebreaker priority: (1) rows with real InvMasterSKU win over sentinel/null, (2) active items win over inactive, (3) most recently updated wins. Resolves the 622 duplicate SKUs (1,873 rows = 32% of source). Per Joanna (Jun 5), ProductSKU is the only Item Number source — no merge with BoM-sourced numbers (those sources are unmapped).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Inventory Commodity Code), External ID, Required.

ProductSKU pattern is the primary signal for routing manufactured items to the correct commodity code. The pattern distinguishes:
  - Items starting with 'P-' are printed (RCB decorates the blank)
  - Items without 'P-' prefix that appear as Assy Items in the Engineering BOM Masters are manufactured blanks (RCB cuts/forms the cup/sleeve from raw stock)
Body pattern then picks sleeve vs cup geometry. This rule runs after ProductGroupName edge-case routing (Apparel-Outsource and Warehoused) and before the Engineering BOM Masters.Item Type rules for raw materials.

The same ProductSKU field also feeds Item Number — that is a one-to-many mapping where the same source feeds two target fields via different transformations.

External ID format: per schema doc, the lookup expects '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'. Division 2 prefix applied to all values (e.g., '2_RCB-PRINT-CUP').
transformations:
Apply for items in Products or as Assy Items in the Engineering BOM Masters, after ProductGroupName routing has run:

  WHEN ProductSKU starts with 'P-':
      IF body matches /(DWS|DKS|CWS|CKS|WSC)/  → '2_RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE'
      OTHERWISE                                → '2_RCB-PRINT-CUP'

  WHEN SKU is an Assy Item in the Engineering BOM Masters AND does NOT start with 'P-' (manufactured blank):
      IF body matches /(DWS|DKS|CWS|CKS|WSC)/  → '2_RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE'
      OTHERWISE                                → '2_RCB-BLANK-CUP'  (covers WHC08/12/16/20, CHC*, B-CHC*, etc.)

External ID format follows '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'. All outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(100), Required.

Free-text product description from the Products file (RCB's item master). Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call, this is the sole source of item descriptions — the Engineering BOM Masters description sources (Assy Desc, Item) have been unmapped, since every item appears in Products.
transformations: Trim whitespace. Truncate to Rootstock's Item Description max length. Products.ProductName is the only description source (BoM description sources are unmapped per Joanna, Jun 5).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Inventory Commodity Code), External ID, Required.

Product category in the source system, with 18 distinct values such as 20WHC, DWS, Pad, Warehoused, and Apparel-Outsource. For most items the commodity code is determined by SKU pattern rather than this field, but two ProductGroupName values trigger important commodity code routings: 'Apparel-Outsource' routes items to RCB-APPAREL-DROP, and 'Warehoused' routes them to RCB-STOCK-RESALE.
transformations:
Apply this rule first, before SKU-pattern routing:

  WHEN ProductGroupName = 'Apparel-Outsource' → '2_RCB-APPAREL-DROP'
  WHEN ProductGroupName = 'Warehoused'        → '2_RCB-STOCK-RESALE'

For any other ProductGroupName value, fall through to the SKU-pattern rule (ProductSKU → Inventory Commodity Code) and the Engineering BOM Masters.Item Type rule.

External ID format follows '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'. All outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2).

entries.explanation: Supplier brand name (YBC, PLUS, RCB, or Radix). These are RCB's house brands and supplier identifiers, not Rootstock Vendor records. The field belongs on Vendor, Approved Vendor List, or Vendor Item tables, which are separate target objects not included in the current Engineering Item Master and Inventory Commodity Code migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future Vendor migration phase.

entries.explanation: Last-modified timestamp from the source system. Rootstock maintains its own audit timestamps, so legacy timestamps generally are not useful in the new system.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Manufactured, Purchased, Subcontract}, Optional (inherits from commodity code if blank).

Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call, RCB uses only Manufactured and Purchased — no Subcontract. The rule is simple: if a SKU has a Bill of Materials (appears as an Assy Item in Engineering BOM Masters) it is Manufactured; everything else is Purchased.

Data observation (retained for reference): the source contains two sentinel values in InvMasterSKU — 'NO INVENTORY' (376 rows, typically one-off custom orders) and 'OUTSOURCED' (1,378 rows / 1,275 unique SKUs, drop-ship apparel filed under ProductGroupName='20WHC'). Under Joanna's simplified rule, both sentinel groups resolve to Purchased (they have no BoM). This is a change from the prior spec, which routed OUTSOURCED to Subcontract.
transformations:
Per Joanna (Rootstock PS), Jun 5:

  CASE
    WHEN SKU appears as an Assy Item in Engineering BOM Masters THEN 'Manufactured'
    ELSE 'Purchased'
  END

No Subcontract is used. Note: 'NO INVENTORY' items (376 rows, one-off custom orders) resolve to Purchased under this rule — confirm with RCB whether these should be loaded or filtered out.

entries.explanation: Number of pieces per case (for example, 1,000 sleeves per case). Per the business context document, RCB sells and inventories in cases but manufactures in each, with BOMs structured as Parent Work Orders containing Sub-Assembly Work Orders. ProductCaseQty captures the quantity relationship between the parent (sold by case) and its sub-assembly components (manufactured in each) — i.e., for P-DWS with ProductCaseQty=1000, one case of the parent contains 1,000 sleeve sub-assembly units. This is parent-to-component quantity data; no destination field exists for it on Engineering Item Master or Inventory Commodity Code (which are item-level objects, not relationship objects). Belongs on whichever BoM-relationship target object handles parent-component quantities, which is out of scope for this migration phase.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future BoM-relationship migration phase, where it represents the parent-to-sub-assembly quantity link.

entries.explanation: The selling unit of measure (Case, Single, or Roll). Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call, this is the SELLING UOM and belongs on the Product Master target object in Rootstock — not on the Engineering Item Master. RCB uses the same UOM codes for selling and engineering, but the selling UOM is a distinct field on a distinct object. Product Master is not yet an in-scope target table for this POC. This field will be remapped to Product Master.Selling UOM once Joanna ingests the Product Master table. (A manual mapping to Engineering UOM on PE Item was created during testing; that should be removed since the correct destination is Product Master.)
transformations: No transformation needed for the current target tables. Awaiting ingestion of the Product Master target table, after which this maps to Product Master.Selling UOM.

entries.explanation: Print-shop specific count, likely capturing sheets per case or imposition information. There is no corresponding standard field in the Engineering Item Master or Inventory Commodity Code templates.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If RCB needs this information after migration, add a custom field to the import template.

entries.explanation: Related to ProductSheets — print-shop math specific to the source system. No standard target field exists in Rootstock.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded.

entries.explanation: Numeric foreign key to a product-group lookup in the source system. The relationship between ProductGroupId and ProductGroupName is many-to-many in the source (the same ID can have multiple names, and the same name can have multiple IDs), making this field unreliable for category mapping. Use ProductGroupName instead.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded.

entries.explanation: Free-text notes. About 30% of rows are null, and most non-null values are whitespace. No standard Notes field exists on the Engineering Item Master import template.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If RCB wants to preserve notes, add a custom long-text field to Engineering Item Master and extend the import template.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Pending, Active}, Required.

Lifecycle status of the item. Per Joanna (Rootstock PS) on the Jun 5 call, ProductActive drives Status directly: an active product (ProductActive = 1) maps to Status = Active, and an inactive product (ProductActive = 0) maps to Status = Pending. This is distinct from Inactive Status (the usage flag) — see the ProductActive → Inactive Status mapping. Note: the source file labeled 'Products' is RCB's item master (confirmed by Joanna on the Jun 5 call), so pulling Status from it is correct.
transformations:
Per Joanna (Rootstock PS), Jun 5:

  CASE WHEN Products.ProductActive = 1 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Pending' END

For items sourced only from Engineering BOM Masters with no Products match, default to Status = 'Active'.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Checkbox, Optional (Checked = Inactive; Unchecked = Active or Pending).

Checkbox indicating whether an item is currently in use. Status and Inactive Status are orthogonal: Status is the record lifecycle (Active vs Pending), Inactive Status is the usage flag (FALSE/unchecked = in use, TRUE/checked = retired). The combination Status='Active' with Inactive Status=TRUE represents a legacy item that was once released but is no longer in use — the standard end-of-life state.

Field type caveat: the schema doc shows Checkbox (TRUE/FALSE). The reference template CSV shows a literal 'I' value in this column for an inactive row, suggesting the field may actually accept a single-character code in some org configurations. The transformation uses TRUE/FALSE per the schema; if the live RCB org rejects boolean values, switch to 'I'/blank.
transformations:
Apply this rule only to items sourced from Products:

  CASE WHEN Products.ProductActive = 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END

Items sourced only from the Engineering BOM Masters (no Products match) default to FALSE (active). The field is a Checkbox in Rootstock — values are TRUE (checked = inactive) or FALSE / blank (unchecked = active or pending).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Division Master), External ID, Required.

Engineering Division FK — assigns the Engineering Item Master to a division.
transformations: Constant `2` for all peitems (single-division setup per RCB cleaned file).

entries.explanation:

Item kind on Engineering Item Master (Direct Material / Labor Only). NOTE: Different concept from Engineering BOM Masters.Item Type (Inventory/Non Inventory) — picklists do not align.
transformations: Constant `Direct Material` for all peitems (no labor-only items in RCB data).

Whether lot numbers are tracked at the item level.

entries.explanation:

Whether serial numbers are tracked.

FIFO costing override at item level. Normally inherited from commodity code.

Reverse-BoM (disassembly) item flag.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Division Master), External ID, Required.

Eng Division for the commodity code record.
transformations: Constant `2` for all Inventory Commodity Code rows.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(20), Required.

The commodity code name (primary identifier). One Inventory Commodity Code row per code.
transformations:
Per-code value. Proposed set (11 codes):

Manufactured:
  • RCB-PRINT-CUP        — printed paper hot cups (P-WHC*, P-KIC*, P-CHC*, etc.)
  • RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE     — printed sleeves (P-DWS, P-DKS, P-CWS, P-CKS)
  • RCB-BLANK-CUP        — manufactured blank cups (WHC08/12/16/20, CHC*, B-CHC*, WSC22/32)
  • RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE     — manufactured blank sleeves (if any)

Purchased:
  • RCB-PRINT-MAT        — paper raw materials (PR-* paper sheets)
  • RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK   — inks (A0xxx)
  • RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE  — glues (D0xxx, C0xxx) — split from INK because operationally different
  • RCB-PACKAGING        — boxes, bags, tape, labels, printed instructions (BX-*, BG-*, BC*, N0*, TAPE-*, LABEL-*, BCI)
  • RCB-STOCK-RESALE     — warehoused stock for resale (Products.ProductGroupName = 'Warehoused')
  • RCB-APPAREL-DROP     — drop-ship apparel (InvMasterSKU = 'OUTSOURCED', 1,275 SKUs). NOTE (Jun 5): per Joanna, RCB uses no Subcontract — this code's default Inventory Source is Purchased, not Subcontract. See decisions log; ICC value fields pending dedicated review.

Catch-all:
  • RCB-UNROUTED         — items that did not match any routing rule. Requires user review before load.

External IDs format as '2_<code>' (e.g., '2_RCB-PRINT-CUP') per the division prefix requirement.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(100), Required.

Human-readable description of the commodity code.
transformations:
Per-code value (human-readable):

  RCB-PRINT-CUP        → 'Printed Paper Hot Cups'
  RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE     → 'Printed Cup Sleeves'
  RCB-BLANK-CUP        → 'Manufactured Blank Cups'
  RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE     → 'Manufactured Blank Sleeves'
  RCB-PRINT-MAT        → 'Print Materials — Paper Stock'
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK   → 'Ink Consumables'
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE  → 'Glue Consumables'
  RCB-PACKAGING        → 'Packaging Materials (Boxes, Bags, Tape, Labels)'
  RCB-STOCK-RESALE     → 'Warehoused Stock for Resale'
  RCB-APPAREL-DROP     → 'Drop-Ship Apparel'
  RCB-UNROUTED         → 'Items Requiring Review — Did Not Match Routing Rules'

Buying Division FK.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(1), Required (typically A/B/C).

ABC inventory classification (A=high-value, B=mid, C=low).
transformations:
Per-code (educated guess; RCB should validate via velocity analysis):

  A — RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK-CUP, RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE (high-value finished/blank items)
  B — RCB-PRINT-MAT, RCB-STOCK-RESALE, RCB-APPAREL-DROP (mid-value)
  C — RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK, RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE, RCB-PACKAGING (low-value consumables)
  C — RCB-UNROUTED (default until reviewed)

transformations: Constant `Active`.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Standard, Phantom, Reference}, Optional. NOTE: Schema doc omits this field but the import-template CSV includes it and the Engineering Item Master schema explicitly references "the corresponding field on the Inventory Commodity Code" for Eng Type inheritance — confirming it exists..

Default Eng Type for items assigned to this commodity code.
transformations: Per-code: `Standard` for most codes; `Phantom` only for codes that hold catalog-only sub-assemblies.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Manufactured, Purchased, Subcontract}, Required.

Default Inventory Source for items in this code. NOTE (Jun 5 call): per Joanna, RCB uses only Manufactured and Purchased — no Subcontract. The item-level InvMasterSKU → Inventory Source mapping now reflects this. The per-code defaults below still list RCB-APPAREL-DROP as Subcontract from the prior spec; this should be changed to Purchased to stay consistent. The full set of ICC value-assignment fields was NOT reviewed in the Jun 5 meeting (the call ended at Unit of Measure) and needs a dedicated review pass — see decisions log.
transformations:
Per commodity code:

  Manufactured: RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK-CUP, RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE
  Purchased:    RCB-PRINT-MAT, RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK, RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE, RCB-PACKAGING, RCB-STOCK-RESALE
  Purchased:    RCB-APPAREL-DROP  (changed from Subcontract per Joanna's no-Subcontract rule, Jun 5 — confirm in ICC review)
  Catch-all:    RCB-UNROUTED (set after user review; provisionally Purchased)

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Lot for Lot, Days Cover, Reorder Point, No MRP Planning} — schema notes underlying codes L/D/R/N, Required.

MRP planning strategy for items in this code.
transformations:
Per commodity code:

  Lot for Lot:         RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK-CUP, RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE, RCB-PRINT-MAT
  No MRP Planning:     RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK, RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE, RCB-PACKAGING
  Days Cover:          RCB-STOCK-RESALE
  Lot for Lot:         RCB-APPAREL-DROP
  No MRP Planning:     RCB-UNROUTED (until user reviews and assigns proper code)

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Home Project, Not Home}, Required.

Project home flag — whether inventory for items in this code is held against specific projects vs general stock.

Picklist value caveat: the schema doc shows values 'Home Project' and 'Not Home'. The reference template CSV uses 'Project Home' for the active state (note word order differs). The transformation below uses the schema-doc 'Home Project' value; verify against live RCB org.
transformations:
Per commodity code:
  'Home Project'  for items costed directly to projects
  'Not Home'      for general stock items

Default 'Not Home' unless RCB uses project costing.

If the load rejects 'Home Project', try 'Project Home' (template value, word order reversed).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Direct (including Sub-contract), Indirect, Outside Operation, Service}, Required.

Type of purchase/transaction for items in this commodity code.

Picklist value caveat: the schema doc shows 'Direct (including Sub-contract)' for the direct value. The reference template CSV uses 'Direct Purchases' for the same field. One of the two artifacts is wrong. The mapping below uses the schema-doc value; if the load rejects it, switch to 'Direct Purchases'.

Note: different concept from Engineering Item Master.Item Type (Blank/Direct Material/Labor Only) — picklists do not align across the two objects.
transformations:
Per commodity code, set one of the schema's four picklist values:

  `Direct (including Sub-contract)` for most purchased and manufactured codes
  `Direct (including Sub-contract)` for RCB-APPAREL-DROP (changed from 'Outside Operation' per Joanna's no-Subcontract rule, Jun 5 — confirm in ICC review)

  `Indirect` and `Service` are not used for RCB.

transformations: Leave NULL — RCB has no service-type commodity codes.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {No Backflush, First Op, Last Op}, Required.

When to backflush components from inventory automatically.

Picklist value caveat: the schema documentation lists values as 'No Backflush', 'First Op', 'Last Op'. The reference template CSV from RCB's other Rootstock org uses 'No Backflushing', 'First Operation', 'Last Operation' for the same field. One of the two artifacts is using display labels and the other API values; we cannot determine which the live RCB org accepts without testing. The mapping below uses the schema-doc values; if the load rejects them, switch to the template values.
transformations:
Per commodity code, set one of the schema's three picklist values:

  `First Op` or `Last Op` for manufactured codes (RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE)
  `No Backflush` for purchased codes (RCB-BLANK, RCB-PRINT-MAT, RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK, RCB-PACKAGING, RCB-STOCK-RESALE)
  `No Backflush` for RCB-APPAREL-DROP
